title: 12. In The Case Of Hiten P. Dayal vs Bratindranath on 8 August, 2023
full_text: 12. In The Case Of Hiten P. Dayal vs Bratindranath on 8 August, 2023 IN THE COURT OF MS DIVYA ARORA, MM (NI ACT)-01, SOUTH-WEST DISTRICT: NEW DELHI CC No. 15749/18 Under Section 138 of N.I. Act In the matter of: RELIGARE FINVEST LIMITED Having to Registered Office at: D3, P3B, District Centre, Saket, New Delhi -110 017. Through its Authorized Representative Shri Sonpal Singh ... Complainant Versus GURPREET SINGH ARORA s/o Shri Harvinder Singh Arora GE International 51/8, First floor, Shri Nagar Colony, Bharat Nagar Road, New Delhi - 110 052. R/o 46, Pragati Sheel Apartment, Vasundhara Enclave, Mayur Vihar, Delhi - 110 096. Also at : 24/20, Block -24, Shakti Nagar, Delhi - 110 007. ... Accused Date of Institution : 15.05.2018 Date of Judgment : 08.08.2023 Digitally signed by Divya Divya Arora Arora Date: 2023.08.08 Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 1 to 15 16:17:35 Complaint Case no.15749/2018 +0530 JUDGMENT 1. Briefly, the case of complainant is that accused is the the proprietor of M/S GE International and approached the complainant company for grant of loan facility under Small and Medium Enterprises Loan. It is further alleged that after execution of Loan agreement, accused was provided loan facility of Rs 10 lakhs under Small and Medium Enterprises Loan vide loan agreement no. XSMEPNG00072004. It is further alleged that as per the said loan agreement, accused agreed to repay the said loan amount in equal monthly installments. Thereafter, accused failed to comply with the terms and conditions of loan agreement. It is further alleged that in discharge of his legal liability, accused issued a Cheque bearing no. 518691 dated 31.03.2018 for Rs.419787/- drawn on IDBI Bank Ltd, Aggarwal Central, Plaza Plot no.11, Sector 5, Dwarka, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to Cheque in question) and assured the complainant that the cheque would be honoured on its presentation. However, on presentation of the Cheque, the same was returned dishonoured vide return memo dated 04.04.2018 with the remarks ''Funds Insufficient''. Upon this, the complainant sent a legal demand notice dated 13.04.2018 to the accused. On failure of accused to pay the cheque amount within the mandatory period of 15 days, the complainant has moved this court with a complaint under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter referred as " NI Act "). Copy of Power of Attorney is Ex.CW1/A and power of attorney and board of resolution are Ex. CW1/A1 (colly) OSR, Original Cheque is Ex.CW1/B, Return memo is Digitally signed by Divya Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 2 to 15 Arora Date: 2023.08.08 Complaint Case no.15749/2018 16:17:44 +0530 Ex.CW1/C, Copy of Legal Notice is Ex.CW1/D, Original postal receipts are Ex.CW1/E1 to Ex.CW1/E2 and Tracking report is Ex.CW1/F1 and Ex.CW1/F2. 2. On finding of prima facie case against the accused, summons were issued against him and accused appeared before the court on 20.03.2019. 3. The notice under section 251 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (" Cr.P.C .") was framed against the accused vide order dated 07.04.2021 to which he pleaded not guilty. He deposed that, "It was a security Cheque given to complainant company. I have not filled the particulars on the Cheque in question. Complainant company has filled the particulars on the Cheque in question. I was never informed that the complainant company is going to present the Cheque. The Cheque in question bears my signatures. I do not remember whether I received the legal notice." 4. The complainant adopted his pre-summoning evidence tendered by way of affidavit as his post-summoning evidence. 5. After framing of notice, AR of complainant company was examined in chief as CW1 and was cross examined by ld counsel for accused at full length. Thereafter, CE was closed and the matter was listed for statement of accused under Section 313 CrPC. Divya Arora Digitally signed by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:17:51 +0530 Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 3 to 15 Complaint Case no.15749/2018 6. Statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 CrPC read with Section 281 Cr.P.C. on 11.01.2023 wherein all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence against the accused was put to her to which she stated that, "I do not remember the exact loan agreement number and application ID number. I have already repaid approximately Rs.7 lacs through EMIs. All the EMIs were paid through bank transfers. There was default in making the payment of 1 to 2 EMIs. Complainant company presented my security cheques despite seeking of time for repayment by me. The Cheque in question bears my signatures. It was given as security Cheque at the time of loan agreement. I had not filled the particulars on the Cheque in question. I did not receive any legal notice. However, the Shakti Nagar address mentioned on the legal notice is correct. I was residing at Shakti Nagar address till September 2018. I do not owe liability of Cheque amount. I am willing to clear my loan account if complainant company ask for reasonable amount." 7. Accused led the evidence in his defence and examined Shri Abhinav Vyas, Assistant Manger, IDBI Bank as DW1. Thereafter, DE was closed vide Order dated 26.04.2023. 8. Thereafter, the Ld. Counsel for complainant and the accused were heard at length and the matter was reserved for Judgment. 9. Before proceeding to the merits of the case, it is important to lay down the basic provision of law with respect to Section 138 NI Act which is as follows:- Section 138 of Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 4 to 15 Digitally signed Complaint Case no.15749/2018 by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:00 +0530 Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 makes dishonour of cheques an offence. It provides that ''where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability, is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall without prejudice to any other provisions of this Act, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both''. 10. In order to ascertain whether the accused has committed on offence u/s 138 NI Act, the following ingredients constituting the offence have to be proved:- (a) The drawer of the cheque should have issued the cheque for the discharge, in whole or in part of a legally enforceable debt or other liability. (b) The cheque is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank. Divya Arora Digitally signed by Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 5 to 15 Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:08 +0530 Complaint Case no.15749/2018 (c) The drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money within fifteen days of the receipt of the notice from the payee or the holder in due course demanding the payment of the said amount of money. It is only when all the above mentioned ingredients are satisfied that the person who has drawn the cheque can be set to have committed an offence u/s 138 NI Act. 11. It is important to recall Section 118 of the Indian Evidence Act 1872 and Section 139 of the N.I Act here. Section 118 (a) of the Act provides that until the contrary is proved, it shall be presumed that ''that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred, was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration''. Further, Section 139 of the Act lays down that ''it shall be presumed, unless the contrary is provided, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section 138 for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability. 12. In the case of Hiten P. Dayal Vs Bratindranath Bannerjee (2001) G SCC 16, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India had observed that ''Because both sections 138 and 139 CrPC required that the court shall presume the liability of the drawer of the cheque for the amount for which the cheques are drawn as noted in State of Madras Vs A. Vaidhyanatha Iyer AIR 1958 SC 61, it is obligatory on the court that raise this presumption in every case where the factual basis for raising of Divya Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 6 to 15 Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Digitally signed by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:17 +0530 the presumption has been established. It introduces an exception to the general rule as to the burden of proof in criminal cases and shifts the onus on to the accused''. 13. The core issue that arises for consideration whether the cheque in question was issued by the accused in discharge of his liability. 14. The accused has admitted his signatures on the cheque in question at the stage of notice framed u/s 251 , Cr.P.C. and examination u/s 313 , Cr.P.C. Thus, unless the contrary is proved, it shall be presumed that the complainant received the cheque in discharge of the debt/ liability from the accused. The standard of proof for rebuttal is on preponderance of probabilities. As held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in decision cited as K.N. Beena vs Muniyappan And Another ;(2001) 8 SCC 458, in order to rebut the presumption, mere denial by the accused will not suffice. The accused must prove by leading cogent evidence that there was no debt/ liability. 15. Major defence led by accused is that cheque in question was given as a security cheque at the time of availing loan facility from complainant company. In support of his defence, accused got DW2 (Bank official from IDBI Bank) summoned to show that cheque in question along with other cheques of same series were given to complainant as security. 16. The defence of security cheques is no longer a grey area. It was held in the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 7 to 15 Digitally signed Complaint Case no.15749/2018 by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:25 +0530 V. S. Yadav v. Reena CRL A. No. 1136 Of 2010 that: "Mere pleading not guilty and stating that the cheques were issued as security, would not amount to rebutting the presumption raised under Section 139 of N.I. Act. The Accused, by cogent evidence, has to prove the circumstance under which cheques were issued". 17. Further, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Suresh Chand Goyal vs Amit Singhal (2015) 2 DLT (Cri) 803 held that : "The contention that the cheque was issued only as security is preposterous. The cheque whether issued for payment of debt or as security makes no distinction in law. The cheque is a negotiable instrument, it may be that sometimes the cheque is issued with a request on the part of the drawer to defer the presentation of the cheque for some time to enable the drawer to make payment by cash and take back the cheque or allow time to arrange funds for encashment of cheque. When the amount is not paid as per oral understanding the payee is well justified to present the cheque for encashment. The cheque even if it is issued as a security for payment, it is negotiable instrument and encashable security at the hands of payee. Therefore, merely because the drawer contends that it is issued as security is not a ground to exonerate the penal liability under Sec.138 of the NI Act". 18. The defence raised by the accused that the cheque in question was given as security, hence, not covered within the meaning of Section 138 NI Act is devoid of merit as a cheque given as security is also covered u/s 138 NI Act, if on the date of presentment of such a cheque, valid legal debt/liability persists. In this regard law has been settled in view of the authoritative Divya Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 8 to 15 Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Digitally signed by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:34 +0530 pronouncement by the Hon'ble Apex Court in ICDS Ltd vs. Beena Shabeer 2002 (2) SCC 426 ,where it was held that:- "Security cheques would also fall within the purview of the Section 138 NI Act and a person cannot escape his liability unless he proves that debt or liability for which cheque was issued as security is satisfied otherwise." 19. Accused has averred that he has not filled the particulars on the cheque in question. In Oriental Bank of Commerce V. Prabodh Kumar Tewari Crl . Appeal no.1260 of 2022 it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that, "For such a determination, the fact that the details of the Cheque have been filled up not by the drawer, but by some other person would be immaterial. The presumption which arises on the signing of the Cheque cannot be rebutted merely by the report of a hand-writing expert. Even if the details in the Cheque have not been filled by drawer but by another person, this is not relevant to the defence whether Cheque was issued towards payment of a debt or in discharge of a liability." 20. Even if for the sake for the arguments, it is believed that cheque in question was blank but the fact that the Cheque is in possession of the complainant with no plausible explanation coming from accused to show as to how has he cleared his loan account. Further, inaction on the part of accused to take steps for stopping misuse or wrong encashment of his cheque by complainant suggests that he never took steps to procure back his alleged blank signed cheque. Section 20 of the NI Act provides Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 9 to 15 Digitally signed by Divya Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:46 +0530 that if a person signs and delivers a paper stamped in accordance with the loan and either wholly blank or have written thereon an incomplete negotiable instrument, such person thereby gives prima facie authority to the holder thereof to make or complete, as the case may be, a negotiable instrument for any amount specified therein and not exceeding the amount covered by the stamp. 21. Another argument raised by Ld counsel for accused is that there is no resolution passed by board of directors to show authorisation in favour of director Mr. Mohit Kapoor, who executed SPA in favour of Mr. Sonpal Singh. He further argued complainant has admitted in his cross examination that there is no resolution on record to prove legal notice and present complaint was filed with proper authorization. He further relied upon judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in State Bank of Travancore V M/S Kingston Computer (I) Pvt. Ltd. (2011) 11 SCC 524. In this aforementioned case, Apex Court reversed the order passed by Division bench of Hon'ble High court of Delhi, on the ground of no resolution being passed by board of directors in favour of director of company, to authorise another person to file a suit on behalf of the company. 22. Coming to facts of present case, it is correct that at the stage of pre-summoning, previous AR had filed only SPA and not any resolution passed by board of directors authorising Sh. Mohit Kapoor to appoint any attorney on behalf of complainant company. This court is of the opinion that there was no need of filing the resolution at the stage of pre-summoning evidence. At Digitally signed by Divya Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 10 to 15 Divya Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:18:55 +0530 the stage of post summoning evidence, AR was substituted and special power of attorney along with resolution passed by board of directors was filed on record, exhibited as Ex. CW1/A1. Perusal of Ex. CW1/A1 reveals that a resolution dated 07.11.2019 was passed by board of directors authorising Nishant Singhal and other persons to represent the company as its lawful attorney. Further, the same resolution also gave power to Nishant Singhal and other authorised signatories to execute a power of attorney, empowering any employee of the company to do all the acts mentioned in the resolution. Nishant Singhal, being an authorised signatory, authorised Arun Mohan to represent the company vide SPA dated 08.01.2020. Merely because resolution is not filed on record with regard to previous director and AR, accused cannot discredit the entire case of complainant. Had complainant not filed the resolution in favour of substituted AR, the outcome would have been different. Complainant has no where denied the execution of resolution in favour of previous director, who authorised previous AR. It is only that it was not filed at the stage of pre- summoning evidence. If accused had any objection with regard to authenticity of resolution or non filing of previous resolution, he should have called for the minutes of meeting of the board of directors. Hence, this defence and judgment relied upon by accused does not help in discharging the burden of proof. 23. The complainant has been able to establish that the cheque in question was issued by the accused for discharge of his legally enforceable liability. There is no rebuttal brought on record by the accused by way or oral / documentary evidence and Digitally signed by Divya Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 11 to 15 Divya Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:19:03 +0530 hence, the foremost ingredients of offence punishable u/s 138 of NI Act has been proved beyond reasonable doubt against the accused. Accused has not filed any cogent evidence to show how has he cleared his loan account with complainant company. 24. Therefore, considering the weight of the attending circumstances viz, the consistency in the prosecution story, and the failure of the accused to put forth any reasonable and believable defence and fact that the accused has not proved his defence to cause the probabilities to lie in his favour, an element of section 138 NI Act stands assembled. 25. Another condition with regard to Section 138 NI Act is receiving of legal notice. Accused has denied to the receiving of legal notice at the stage of notice framed under Section 251 CrPC and statement recorded u/s 313 CrPC ,however, in the same statement, he has admitted that he was residing at Shakti Nagar address till September 2018. The legal notice in the present case was sent on 13.04.2018. This court is of the view that the address on the legal notice once having been shown to be the correct address of accused and legal notice having been dispatched by registered AD, a presumption of due service arises in view of Section 27 of General Clause Act & Section 114 of Indian Evidence Act and now it is upon accused to prove that notice was not served upon him. Not even an iota of evidence has been brought on record by the accused to displace the presumption of due service. To the contrary, perusal of record shows that complainant has issued a legal demand notice to the accused and same was dispatched by way of speed post. Divya Arora Digitally signed Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 12 to 15 by Divya Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Date: 2023.08.08 16:19:11 +0530 26. Also in CC Alavi Haji Vs. Palapatti Mohammad (Crl.)767/2007 the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India held that "where the notice is sent by Registered post by correctly addressing the drawer of the cheque, the mandatory requirement of issue of notice in terms of clause (b) of proviso to section 138 Act stands complied with." Further, the above judgment also stated that any drawer who claims that he did not receive the notice sent by post, can within 15 days of receipt of summons from the court in respect of the complaint u/s 138 NI Act make payment of the cheque amount and submit to the court that he had made payment within 15 days of receipt of summons. In the present case, the accused has failed to adduce any evidence to rebut the presumption of due service. As such, the legal notice stood served upon the accused. 27. Another condition qua the presentation of the cheque within three months is concerned, the same is satisfied upon the perusal of the cheque in question dated 31.03.2018 (Ex.CW1/B) while the return memo 04.04.2018 (Ex.CW1/C) thus, being presented within the prescribed period of limitation of three months. The defence did not adduce any evidence whatsoever to contradict the same. 28. Another condition pertains to the cheque being returned unpaid owing to their being dishonored. Bank return memo or slip is prima facie proof of dishonor. Section 146 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, in this regard comes into play which raises a presumption that the court shall presume the fact Divya Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 13 to 15 Arora Complaint Case no.15749/2018 Digitally signed by Divya Arora Date: 2023.08.08 16:19:19 +0530 of dishonor of the cheque in case of cheque is returned vide a return memo issued by the bank having thereon the official mark denoting that the cheque has been dishonored. Again, as the defence has failed to rebut the said presumption, hence the said condition is also satisfied. 29. The last condition is that accused fails to make the payment within fifteen days from the date of the receipt of the legal demand notice. In the present case, the accused has evidently failed to make the payment within the fifteen days contending that she owes no legal liability to pay the amount mentioned in the cheque in question. The accused has miserably failed to prove that said assertion and thus, the last limb of what will entail the liability against the accused, is also structured. 30. In view of the forgoing discussion, the accused has miserably failed in probabilising her defence, even on the scale of preponderance of probabilities. 31. The complainant has with the aid of evidence led a presumption of legal liability under Section 118 read with Section 139 of N. I. Act and has successfully proved the basic ingredients of offence under section 138 N. I Act. 32. Resultantly, the accused Gurpreet Singh Arora stands convicted for the offence under Section 138 NI Act. Let the convict be heard separately on the quantum of sentence. Divya Arora Digitally signed by Divya Arora Religare Finvest Limited v. Gurpreet Singh Arora Page number 14 to 15 Date: 2023.08.08 Complaint Case no.15749/2018 16:19:27 +0530 33. Let a digitally signed copy of the Judgment be supplied to the accused, free of cost, and a copy of the same be placed on record.
